input.question: What year was the Married Women's Property Act passed?

documents.text: Married Women's Property Act 1882 The Married Women's Property Act 1882 (45 & 46 Vict. c.75) was an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that significantly altered English law regarding the property rights of married women, which besides other matters allowed married women to own and control property in their own right. The Act applied in England (and Wales) and Ireland, but did not extend to Scotland. The Married Women’s Property Act was a model for similar legislation in other British territories.
